name: a_software_security
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Software & cybersecurity.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
SaaS and cybersecurity company news, analyst notes and PT changes, AI-agent impact on software seats and pricing, sector ETF (IGV) move and drivers.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **PTC** `[Software & SaaS]`
- Schneider Electric agreed on October 5 to acquire PTC for **$205 per share** in cash, valuing PTC’s equity at approximately **$22.6 billion** and its enterprise value at **$23.7 billion**; the offer represents a **42.3% premium** to PTC’s October 2 close, with closing expected in **Q3 2027**. (Reuters, Oct 5 06:48 ET)[3]
- PTC shares rose **37% in pre-market trading** on October 5 after the transaction announcement. (Reuters, Oct 5 06:20 ET)[2]

## **IGV** `[Software & SaaS]`
- The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (**IGV**) closed at **$108.43**, up **$0.20**, or **0.18%**, on Friday, October 2 at **16:00 ET**. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2 16:00 ET)[10]
- IGV was quoted at **$108.47**, up **$0.04**, or **0.04%**, in the latest reported reading. (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2 16:00 ET)[10]
- IGV had gained **3.9% over the preceding three weeks** as of October 5. (Philstar, Oct 5 08:33 ET)[4]
- IGV and the semiconductor ETF SOXX were each reported to be up **more than 2% for the week** ending October 2. (Macro4Micro, Oct 5 06:48 ET)[7]
- The October 5 pre-market software-sector backdrop included lower U.S. equity-index futures, with Dow futures down **101 points**, or **0.2%**, and S&P 500 futures down **14.25 points**, or **0.18%**, at **06:20 ET**. (Reuters, Oct 5 06:20 ET)[2]

## **Software and AI-agent impact** `[Software & SaaS]`
- A report published October 1 and updated October 2 said IGV opened 2026 near **$106**, fell below **$75** in April—approximately a **30% decline**—and traded near **$105** by mid-September. (Business Insider, Oct 2 13:59 ET)[8]
- The same report described the 2026 software selloff as driven by concerns that **agentic AI could disrupt traditional enterprise software**, while noting that the ETF had recovered to approximately its early-2026 level by mid-September. (Business Insider, Oct 2 13:59 ET)[8]

## **Palo Alto Networks / CrowdStrike / Fortinet** `[Cybersecurity]`
- Palo Alto Networks closed at **$397.31** on September 30, CrowdStrike at **$264.75**, and Fortinet at **$178.76**; the October 5 report attributed cybersecurity demand to AI-enabled hybrid attacks involving **China and Russia**. (Adalytica, Oct 5 00:43 ET)[13]
- The same report listed the 200-day-average comparisons as **$248.23** for Palo Alto Networks, **$152.10** for CrowdStrike, and **$117.60** for Fortinet. (Adalytica, Oct 5 00:43 ET)[13]

## **Software sector breadth and names** `[Software & SaaS]`
- A market commentary published October 5 said Intuit, Adobe, FactSet, and Salesforce were among the software and SaaS stocks in the lower-performing group for the prior week. (Macro4Micro, Oct 5 06:48 ET)[7]
- A separate October 5 report said **22.9% of S&P 500 stocks** were above their 50-day moving average. (Philstar, Oct 5 08:33 ET)[4]
- Rubrik was reported at a market value of approximately **$24.4 billion**, with a **36.0% one-month gain** and a **43.9% one-year gain** as of October 2. (Trefis, Oct 5 07:58 ET)[6]

## **Market / rates backdrop** `[Macro / Calendar]`
- U.S. stock-index futures declined on October 5 as technology stocks retreated from record levels; at **06:20 ET**, Dow E-minis were down **0.2%** and S&P 500 E-minis were down **0.18%**. (Reuters, Oct 5 06:20 ET)[2]
- Reuters reported that the prior Friday’s weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs data reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike at the October meeting; the report did not provide a new software-specific analyst target or rating action. (Reuters, Oct 5 06:20 ET)[2]
